# The descriptive sweep — three size-distribution families, one axis each

*Generated by `sweep_descriptive.py` from shards already on disk. No new cells.*
*Every number below is printed by that script into `out/sweep_descriptive.txt`;
none of them is typed here by hand.*

## What was run

Three size-distribution families — lognormal, uniform, bidisperse — over CV 0.0–0.5, at matched friction `mu_p` = 0.3, N = 1500, on a four-rung reduced-pressure ladder. 217 converged cells survive the matched-condition filter; the counts before and after every filter are in the artifact.

## The result

The largest **resolved** across-family contrast is **phi_J**, whose paired CV 0 → 0.5 change spans a factor **4.47×** between the three families (lognormal +0.0621±0.0026, uniform +0.0242±0.0008, bidisperse +0.0139±0.0025). It is the **only** channel that survives all three gates. Read the number as a bracket, not a point: against the furthest CV rung instead of the endpoint it is **2.89×**, and weighting each seed by its own fit uncertainty instead of equally it is **5.51×**. Every family change here rests on 3 seeds.

| observable | lognormal | uniform | bidisperse | across-family spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| phi_J | +0.0620718±0.002555 | +0.0242013±0.0008047 | +0.0138885±0.002485 | 4.47x  RESOLVED |
| Z_all | -2.17689±0.08271 | -2±0.06703 | -2.19378±0.03619 | 1.10x  NOT RESOLVED (the families are not shown to differ: F p = 0.1433) |
| Z_nr (k=2) | -0.189131±0.02838 | -0.0812017±0.01622 | -0.117196±0.03932 | 2.33x  NOT RESOLVED (the families are not shown to differ: F p = 0.0999) |
| rattler fraction | +0.408222±0.01247 | +0.382667±0.01186 | +0.417111±0.003318 | 1.09x  NOT RESOLVED (the families are not shown to differ: F p = 0.1176) |
| contact force mean | +0.000916541±6.851e-05 | +0.00106165±5.799e-05 | +0.0012091±2.738e-05 | 1.32x  NOT RESOLVED (the QUOTED pair is not separated: Welch t = 3.97 against a selection-calibrated 5.95; the nominal 3.46 would have passed it) |
| contact force CV | +0.362127±0.007794 | +0.123075±0.0114 | +0.0433994±0.01332 | UNDETERMINED (denominator) |

A ratio is **RESOLVED** only if all three hold: its smallest family change is non-zero at *t*(df), a conservative heterogeneity test says the three families differ at all, **and** the specific max-vs-min pair the ratio quotes is separated on its own Welch *t* against a **selection-calibrated** threshold. An omnibus *F* says *some* pair differs, which is not the same claim; and because the pair is the argmax/argmin *of the data*, a nominal *t* critical value under-corrects — its measured false-positive rate under the global null is 12–21%, not 5%. Earlier drafts applied one gate, then two, then three with the wrong threshold on the third.

**"NOT RESOLVED" here means undetermined at three seeds, not shown to be absent.** With n = 3 per family the heterogeneity and pairwise gates both have limited power, so a real moderate effect has two chances to miss significance for reasons that are about the replication and not about the effect. `Z_nr`'s F = 3.47, p = 0.0999 is exactly the shape of a true-but-underpowered result.

Printed to six significant figures, not four decimals: `contact force mean` is O(1e−3) and its between-family differences are the size of a 4-decimal rounding quantum, so a reader reconstructing its heterogeneity *F* from the rounded digits got *p* = 0.118 where the full-precision value is 0.0248 — opposite sides of 5%, on a row this table calls RESOLVED. **A number in a claims table that cannot be recomputed from what is printed is not published.**

(CV 0 → 0.5 change, at `p_hat` = 1e-3 for the per-cell channels and extrapolated to `p_hat` → 0 for `phi_J`.)

### How far the ordering can be pushed — and it is not far

Ranked by across-family spread, each marked with whether it survives **both** gates — a denominator that is non-zero at 95% *and* a heterogeneity test that says the families differ at all. Only the marked-RESOLVED ones are quotable: **contact force CV** 8.34× *(not resolved)* > **phi_J** 4.47× *(resolved)* > **Z_nr (k=2)** 2.33× *(not resolved)* > **contact force mean** 1.32× *(not resolved)* > **Z_all** 1.10× *(not resolved)* > **rattler fraction** 1.09× *(not resolved)*.

**That six-way ordering survives only 32% of 20,000 resamples** in which each family change is redrawn as *t*(df = n−1) around its own mean and se. It is not a result. The links that do hold are the individual ones: `contact force CV` > `phi_J` 88%; `phi_J` > `Z_nr (k=2)` 81%; `Z_nr (k=2)` > `contact force mean` 95%; `contact force mean` > `Z_all` 90%; `Z_all` > `rattler fraction` 58%.

Three separate reasons the headline has to be stated weakly, all raised by an adversarial referee against an earlier draft of this page:

1. **The significance guard was wrong.** Each change comes from 3 seeds, so its se carries 2 degrees of freedom and the 95% critical value is *t* = 4.303, not 2. A flat 2·se bar is an 18% test, and it admitted exactly the change that set the denominator of the largest ratio. The guard is now *t*(df = n−1), **and a second gate was added beside it**: the denominator test asks whether the smallest family's change is non-zero, which is not the question the ordering needs — that question is whether the families differ *from each other*.
2. **The endpoint definition does real work, on every channel including the one carrying the headline.** CV 0 → 0.5 assumes monotonicity and the bidisperse family is not monotone. Against the furthest rung instead: `phi_J` 2.89×, `Z_all` 1.10×, `Z_nr (k=2)` 2.06×, `rattler fraction` 1.09×, `contact force mean` 1.32×, `contact force CV` 3.77×. The first version of this check silently **skipped `phi_J`**, which has no shard getter — so the channel now carrying the headline was the only one never checked. These peak ratios are maxima over five noisy estimates and each family is taken at its own best rung, so they are **upper bounds biased high**, not point estimates; they bracket the endpoint number rather than replacing it.
3. **`Z_all` is not an independent channel.** It equals `(1 − rattler_frac)·Z_nr` to within 0.0347 on every one of the 217 cells (the worst over the printed ROWS, which are means over seeds at one rung, is 0.0147 — a row max cannot bound a cell), so its near-family-independence is *inherited* from the rattler fraction's and is not a second confirmation of anything.

### Do the families differ at all? Two tests, both computed

| observable | Cochran Q | p(Q) | ANOVA F | p(F) | differ at 5%? Q / F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| phi_J | 227.78 | 0.0000 | 144.68 | 0.0000 | yes / yes |
| Z_all | 6.56 | 0.0376 | 2.73 | 0.1433 | yes / no |
| Z_nr (k=2) | 10.95 | 0.0042 | 3.47 | 0.0999 | yes / no |
| rattler fraction | 8.07 | 0.0177 | 3.12 | 0.1176 | yes / no |
| contact force mean | 18.59 | 0.0001 | 7.29 | 0.0248 | yes / yes |
| contact force CV | 568.76 | 0.0000 | 224.33 | 0.0000 | yes / yes |

Q treats the printed se's as exactly known, which they are not — each has 2 dof — so it is the **liberal** end and it is measurably anti-conservative here. The one-way ANOVA *F*, reconstructed from the same (mean, se, n) triplets, is the conservative counterpart, and **it had to be computed rather than described**: an earlier draft printed Q alone and put the conservative end in prose, so its "differ at 5%?" column read as six unanimous rejections of family-independence. Conservatively it is 3 of 6: `phi_J`, `contact force mean`, `contact force CV`.

## What it does not say

- **The bidisperse column is a path, not a family.** It is 50:50 *by number*, so its fines carry 0.500 → 0.036 of the volume across this ladder: it never visits the composition where interstitial filling peaks. Matched binaries that differ only in which atom carries the volume pack 0.0635 apart.
- **A spread is not a pairwise separation.** These ratios say the families differ; they do not say two of them can be told apart at a given CV.
- **Only `phi_J` is extrapolated.** `Z`, the rattler fraction and the force moments are read *at* a pressure and move with the rung; the artifact prints all four rungs so the rung dependence is visible rather than chosen.
- **RETRACTED 2026-09-17: the replicate-count footnote.** Earlier versions of this report explained the `(6)` in the lognormal and uniform CV 0.4–0.5 cells as replicates "left over from an earlier campaign" and said nothing was affected. That diagnosis was wrong on both halves. They were not extra seeds: the record key carries the iteration cap, so a cell re-run at the raised cap survived the key dedup twice, and the six-record cells are three seeds counted twice each. And something was affected — the standard errors of exactly those cells, by a factor `sqrt(2.5)` = 1.581, because the duplicated records are bit-identical and shrink the spread without adding information. `load_shards` now collapses one physical cell per (family, CV, seed, `p_hat`) with the higher cap kept, which is the rule `load_fits` has used since 2026-09-08; every count in the tables above is a seed count again. The paired shifts and `phi_J` never went through this path and did not move.

## Ladder health

`phi_J` is a four-rung extrapolation, and a 2026-09-13 review found an arm whose `phi_J` came from ladders that were 0/6 monotone. The same gate is applied here before any `phi_J` is quoted: **lognormal** passes, **uniform** passes, **bidisperse** passes.
